Esa’s Dirty Mix

The soil came first. The store grew out of it.

Before there was a storefront, there was a bag of Esa’s nutrient-rich houseplant blend at the farmers market. Customers kept saying the same thing reviewers still say: the plants they repotted in it took off.

Now it’s a refill program. Reuse. Refill. Replant. Bring your empty Esa’s bag back, walk out with fresh mix and $4 back in your pocket.

All about Esa

A soil blend, a farmers-market table, and then a red door.

Esa is Alisa — the hands and heart behind the Dirty Mix. She started by selling her own houseplant soil blend and stickers (“a place for plant humor and DIRTy talk”), hauling it to markets around the Plateau until the plants needed a permanent home.

In October 2025 she announced a storefront on Cole Street. The signs went up in November, the doors opened for a grand-opening weekend in January 2026, and the place filled up fast: tropical plants floor to ceiling, reclaimed wood, a rotating cast of local makers, and a playlist of throwback jams the plants have apparently been conditioned to prefer.

    Esa’s Dirty Mix launches: premium houseplant soil, sold at markets and from a stand out on Highway 169.

  • Oct 2025

    “BIG NEWS — get ready, Enumclaw.” A storefront on Cole Street.

  • Nov 2025

    Signs are up. The logo hides its little secret in plain sight.

  • Jan 10–11, 2026

    Grand-opening weekend: a build-your-own trucker-hat bar, makers in the pop-up spot, and a town that showed up.

  • Summer 2026

    An artisan at the Enumclaw Plateau Farmers Market, longer summer hours, a bag-refill program, and the first run of Esa’s hoodies and tees.

  • Now

    Open five days a week, shelves still filling up.
